finding.claim: Unvalidated subscriber callbackUrl is stored via subscribe() and later used as the target of server-side POST requests in notifyAll(), enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl), reachable via POST /subscribe (src/Jobs.java:12-14).
finding.sink: client.send(req, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()) at src/Jobs.java:24, with the URI from URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21.

trace.note: subscribe() accepts callbackUrl from the caller.
callbackUrl is stored unchanged in the static subscriptions map.
notifyAll() iterates subscriptions.values() on each scheduled run.
URI.create(cb) parses the attacker-supplied string with no checks.
POST body is the payload string, sent to the attacker-chosen URI.
client.send issues the request from the server's network position; response body is discarded.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, port, IP, loopback, link-local, or RFC 1918 allow/deny check on the path. HttpClient only permits http/https schemes (not a SSRF guard). HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so redirect-based bypass is not possible but the initial request is unrestricted. No DNS resolution check. The /subscribe route handler is not in the repo, so any validation or auth there could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. No scheme, host, IP, or DNS check exists on the path in src/Jobs.java:19-24, and the only grep hits for allowlist/InetAddress/isLoopback terms are the cdn check at src/Jobs.java:30, which governs thumb() and not notifyAll().
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (src/Jobs.java:13-14 store callbackUrl unchecked, and 21-24 send a POST to it), but the attacker-control claim rests only on the comment "POST /subscribe body: name, callbackUrl" at src/Jobs.java:12, and the /subscribe handler that calls subscribe() is not in the repo, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can reach it cannot be verified.
